findings.failure_path: The bounded packet shows only hunks around changed rows, so unchanged locators into the three shifted owner files (llm-inference-integration/SKILL.md, defect-diagnosis/SKILL.md, testing-strategy/SKILL.md) that lie below the insertion points cannot be enumerated. If any such locator existed and was not shifted, the index would silently point a reviewed-semantic obligation at neighboring source text while the shape-only repo audit still exits 0.
findings.smallest_fix: Add to the evidence the total count of locators referencing those three files and the split into shifted (30) versus legitimately unshifted (pre-insertion), so shift completeness is demonstrated rather than only self-consistency.

concern_results.conclusion: Internally consistent with the stated mechanical claim: exactly 26 changed index rows containing 30 changed carrier ranges (llm-inference-integration 4, defect-diagnosis 1, testing-strategy 25), every start and end advancing exactly +2 and every span width preserved (e.g. 122-123 -> 124-125). No obligation ID, proof_mode, disposition, carrier count, qualifier list or non-numeric cell text changes anywhere in the packet, and no carrier path is rewritten. Matches the acceptance that only generated locator line ranges change.

No rule text, gate predicate, threshold, permission, owner assignment or executable appears in the diff; the single touched path is a generated Markdown reader index. No write path, actor or tenant boundary is expressed here, and no mapping row is deleted or retired (O1208 retains its retired-dead row and em-dash carrier unchanged).

Pure locator refresh with no error, concurrency or recovery logic. The only latent partial-failure mode is a partial shift (some post-insertion locators updated, others missed); within the packet every visible locator into the three owner files shifted by +2 and none retained an old value, so no partial-shift contradiction is observable. Whole-file confirmation is not available from the bounded hunks.

The red/green claim (STALE_LEDGER before, exit 0 after, 1240 rows / 0 unresolved) cannot be executed here, but the audit as described validates locator identity, so it would fail with stale locators — the risky behavior in scope. Full make test and hosted CI are explicitly reported pending rather than passed, which is the correct posture. The diff supplies no test artifact of its own; verification rests on the external audit.

Row identity, ordering, schema and canonical mapping references are unchanged, so consumers keyed on obligation IDs or the JSONL mapping are unaffected. No new abstraction or complexity is introduced.

Reverting this partition alone restores the stale index and reproduces the audit failure; it destroys no data since the canonical mapping is the source of truth and the index is regenerable. Nothing here is irreversible.
The index remains a derived reader view; the original failing CI trace and prior receipts are not touched or removed by this diff. No logging or diagnosis surface is changed.

The triggered boundary is ai-output feeding a shared gate: regenerated line numbers could silently re-point a reviewed-semantic obligation at different source text and launder an unreviewed carrier past the audit. Containment is that all 30 deltas are a uniform +2 with preserved spans and unchanged dispositions — a mechanical translation, not a re-selection of carriers. Residual exposure: the audit checks locator shape/identity, not semantic approval, so a wrong-but-well-formed range would still pass; the packet alone cannot exclude that.
